```{r ELECTORAL SYSTEM MAP}
electoral_system_database <-
  read_excel("idea_export_electoral_system_design_database.xlsx") |> 
  group_by(ISO3) |> 
   slice_max(Year) |> 
  ungroup() |> 
  select(ISO3, Country, Year,
         family = `Electoral system family`,
         system = `Electoral system for national legislature`)
 
europe <- 
  ne_countries(scale = "medium", continent = "Europe", returnclass = "sf") |>
  left_join(electoral_system_database, by = c("iso_a3" = "ISO3"))

ggplot(europe) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = family), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(-25, 45), ylim = c(34, 72)) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", na.value = "grey90", name = "Electoral system family") +
  labs(title = "Electoral systems in Europe",
       caption = "Source: IDEA Electoral System Design Database") +
  theme_void()

```

```{r share of each electoral family}
europe |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  count(family) |>
  mutate(pct = round(100 * n / sum(n), 1)) |>
  arrange(desc(n))
```
Maldita from Wayback Machine 
https://maldita.es/malditodato/20240229/partidos-politicos-registro-ministerio-interior/
https://files.maldita.es/uploads/2024/02/65df376828af1informefirma-1706550494955-pdf.pdf#toolbar=0

```{r PARTY REGISTRY}
party_registry_maldita <- read_csv("PARTY_REGISTRY_MALDITA_2024.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)

party_registry_2026 <- read_excel("PARTY_REGISTRY_2026_09.xlsx", col_types = "text") |>
  mutate(new_party = !is.na(registration_date),
         party_id  = cumsum(new_party)) |>
  group_by(party_id) |>
  summarise(party             = str_squish(str_c(party, collapse = " ")),
            address           = first(adress),
            province          = first(province),
            registration_date = first(registration_date),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    party_name        = str_squish(str_remove(party, "\\(([^()]*)\\)$")),
    abbreviation      = str_match(party, "\\(([^()]*)\\)$")[, 2],
    town              = str_squish(str_remove(province, "\\(([^()]*)\\)$")),
    province          = str_match(province, "\\(([^()]*)\\)$")[, 2],
    registration_date = dmy(registration_date),
    status            = "registered"
  ) |>
  select(party_name, abbreviation, registration_date, town, province, address, status)

# parties registered after the 2024 list; some of them were already in it as "not registered"
new_registrations <- party_registry_2026 |>
  filter(registration_date > max(party_registry_maldita$registration_date, na.rm = TRUE))

all_parties <- party_registry_maldita |>
  left_join(new_registrations |>
              select(party_name, new_date = registration_date, province, address),
            by = "party_name") |>
  mutate(registration_date = coalesce(registration_date, new_date),
         status = if_else(!is.na(new_date) & status == "not registered", "registered", status)) |>
  select(-new_date) |>
  bind_rows(new_registrations |> anti_join(party_registry_maldita, by = "party_name")) |>
  arrange(registration_date)
```

FE de las JONS aparece dos veces sin fecha de inscripción: protocolo 21 "(Novillo)" y 22 "(Zulueta)", que son las dos facciones que pidieron la inscripción en 1976. En cambio, party_register la da inscrita el 04/10/1976. Para la fecha de FE de las JONS usa esa.
Alianza Popular (protocolo 961) sale sin fecha de inscripción. Es por cómo lo registra el Ministerio: el PP heredó la inscripción de AP.


```{r TABLE OF FAR RIGHT PARTIES BEFORE VOX}
casals_parties <- c(
  "FUERZA NUEVA", "CENTRO DEMOCRATICO Y SOCIAL", "JUNTAS ESPAÑOLAS", "FRENTE NACIONAL",
  "DEMOCRACIA NACIONAL", "MOVIMIENTO SOCIAL REPUBLICANO",
  "PARTIDO DEL TRABAJO Y EMPLEO-AGRUPACION RUIZ MATEOS \"TRABAJO Y EMPLEO\"",
  "GRUPO INDEPENDIENTE LIBERAL", "SOCIEDAD CIVIL Y DEMOCRACIA", "PLATAFORMA PER CATALUNYA", "ESPAÑA 2000",
  "PARTIDO POR LA LIBERTAD", "ADÑ", "FALANGE ESPAÑOLA DE LAS J.O.N.S.", "LA FALANGE", "FALANGE ESPAÑOLA AUTENTICA",
  "FALANGE AUTENTICA", "FALANGE 2.000", "\"NOSOTROS\" PARTIDO DE LA REGENERACIÓN SOCIAL",
  "ALTERNATIVA ESPAÑOLA", "ALTERNATIVA DE GOVERN", "ALIANZA NACIONAL",
  "SOBERANÍA Y LIBERTAD", "PUEBLO", "FRENTE: NACIONAL IDENTITARIO, PARTIDO NACIONALSOCIALISTA OBRERO ESPAÑOL",
  "SOM IDENTITARIS",
  # Via Democratica, split from PxC in 2010 (Casals); registered under its later name
  "JUNTS PER TABARNIA - VIA DEMOCRÁTICA"
)

casals_registry <- bind_rows(all_parties, party_registry_2026) |>
  filter(party_name %in% casals_parties, !is.na(registration_date)) |>
  group_by(party_name) |>
  slice_min(registration_date, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(party_name, abbreviation, registration_date, cancellation_date) |>
  arrange(registration_date) |> 
  mutate(party = party_name)

far_right_table <- casals_registry |>
  mutate(across(c(registration_date, cancellation_date), \(x) replace_na(format(x, "%d/%m/%Y"), "")),
         abbreviation = replace_na(abbreviation, "")) |>
  select(Party = party_name, Abbreviation = abbreviation,
         Registered = registration_date, Cancelled = cancellation_date)

stargazer(as.data.frame(far_right_table), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Far-right and right-wing populist parties since 1976",
          notes = c("Source: Ministry of the Interior registry of political parties (Maldita 2024; update of September 2026).",
                    "Parties selected following Casals (2020). Cancelled: date the party was struck off the registry."))
```

```{r FAMILY TREE FAR PARTIES 1977-2026}
# every organisation in the links needs a row in the nodes table (must return 0 rows)
tibble(name = unique(c(far_right_links$from, far_right_links$to))) |>
  anti_join(far_right_nodes, by = "name")

# ---- 3. position of each node ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# x = founding year; y = one horizontal band per family
family_order <- c("Francoist dictatorship", "Mainstream right", "Vox", "Coalitions", "Populist radical right",
                  "Identitarian / neo-fascist groups", "Catalan independentist far right",
                  "Neo-Nazi / national-revolutionary", "Neo-Francoism / national-Catholicism", "Falangism")

far_right_nodes <- far_right_nodes |>
  mutate(x    = pmax(founded, 1965L),               # the dictatorship (1939) is drawn at the left edge
         band = match(family, family_order)) |>
  group_by(family) |>
  arrange(x, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  mutate(y = band * 9 + (row_number() %% 5) * 1.6) |>   # stagger names inside each band
  ungroup() |>
  select(-band)

far_right_graph <- tbl_graph(nodes = far_right_nodes, edges = far_right_links, directed = TRUE)

# ---- 4. plot -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
family_colours <- c(
  "Francoist dictatorship"               = "#3B3B3B",
  "Mainstream right"                     = "#1F77B4",
  "Vox"                                  = "#2CA02C",
  "Coalitions"                           = "#7F7F7F",
  "Populist radical right"               = "#FF7F0E",
  "Identitarian / neo-fascist groups"    = "#9467BD",
  "Catalan independentist far right"     = "#E6AB02",
  "Neo-Nazi / national-revolutionary"    = "#000000",
  "Neo-Francoism / national-Catholicism" = "#8C564B",
  "Falangism"                            = "#D62728"
)

ggraph(far_right_graph, layout = "manual", x = x, y = y) +
  geom_edge_arc(aes(colour = type), strength = 0.1,
                arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), type = "closed"),
                end_cap = circle(2.2, "mm"), edge_width = 0.35, alpha = 0.55) +
  geom_node_point(aes(colour = family, fill = if_else(documented, family, "approximate")),
                  shape = 21, size = 3, stroke = 0.9) +
  geom_node_text(aes(label = name, colour = family), size = 2.4, repel = TRUE, max.overlaps = Inf,
                 segment.colour = "grey85", segment.size = 0.2, show.legend = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = family_colours, breaks = family_order, name = NULL) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(family_colours, approximate = "white"), guide = "none") +
  scale_edge_colour_manual(values = c("split / successor"  = "#D62728",
                                      "coalition / merger" = "#1F77B4",
                                      "members / founders" = "grey60"),
                           name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = c(1965, seq(1975, 2025, 5)), labels = c("<1975", seq(1975, 2025, 5)),
                     expand = expansion(add = 2)) +
  scale_y_reverse() +
  labs(title = "Family tree of the Spanish far right, 1975-2026",
       subtitle = "Each arrow goes from an organisation to the one that came out of it, joined a coalition with it or supplied its members. Hollow dots: approximate year",
       caption = "Sources: Ramos (2022), Casals (2020), Wikipedia (Falangist parties)",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey93"),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "bottom", legend.box = "vertical",
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, colour = "grey35"))
```

## General elections

Extraction of general elections candidates: european and general elections via github.com/JaimeObregon/infoelectoral



```{r GITHUB AND INTERIOR MINISTERY PORTAL}
GITHUB <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/JaimeObregon/infoelectoral/main/files"
PORTAL <- "https://infoelectoral.interior.gob.es/estaticos/docxl/apliextr"
```

The github has the files in .DAT, a file type that doesn't separate in ";" or "\|". In order to separate each column, we need to map where the separation between each variable occurs. I asked Claude to give me the exact character positions where the separation is. I used fwf_positions of ReadR to write down the column names, given the positions where the variables lie in the .DAT file.

```{r ADD SOURCE AND PATH OF EACH ELECTION}
elections <-
  elections |>
  mutate(
    folder    = str_c(process, year, month, "_TOTA"),
    code      = str_c(process, str_sub(year, 3, 4), month),
    on_github = !(year %in% c("2023", "2024") |
                    (chamber == "Congress" & year %in% c("1989", "1993"))),
    path      = if_else(on_github,
                        str_c(GITHUB, "/", mirror_folder, "/", folder, "/"),
                        str_c(tempdir(), "/", folder, "/"))
  )

```

```{r DOWNLOAD NON-GITHUB DATA TO TEMPORARY FOLDER}
for (folder in elections$folder[!elections$on_github]) {
  zip_file <- tempfile(fileext = ".zip")
  download.file(str_c(PORTAL, "/", folder, ".zip"), zip_file, mode = "wb",
                method = "libcurl", headers = c("User-Agent" = "Mozilla/5.0"))
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = str_c(tempdir(), "/", folder), junkpaths = TRUE)
}
```

```{r MUTATE AND SELECT VARIABLES OF ALL_CANDIDATES}
    is_titular    = candidate_type == "T",
    is_elected    = elected == "S",
    abbreviation,
    level         = "National",
    .keep = "none"
  )
```

## Autonomical Elections

Claude Code For Autonomical elections: two attempts to confirm it is reproducible.

Prompt 1:

"Quiero que busques todas las listas de todas las elecciones autonómicas que han habido en España desde 2015 hasta 2026 y que pongas en el archivo excel en el excel de CANDIDATOS_AUTONOMICAS. Tienes que ir a la web para recopilar las siguientes variables de cada eleccion: CANDIDATO, CCAA, ELECCION, CIRCUNSCRIPCION, ORDEN, ELEGIDO (TRUE/FALSE)"

Prompt 2:

"You're a Computational Social Scientist. I want you to search for every candidate list of all autonomical elections in Spain from 2015 to 2026 of the following parties: PP and VOX. You have to get into the web and recopilate the following variables for each election:

election: election (write it in like this: "autonomous_2015_05", where 2015 would be the year and 05 the month where the election took place) year: year of the election chamber: the chamber (such as Parlament of Andalucia, Parlament of Catalonia...) province: the province that was being represented by the candidate list_position: the position of the candidate within that list candidate: the candidate's full name is_titular: whether he was the titular of that seat or he was a substitution candidate (TRUE/FALSE), is_elected: whether he was elected (TRUE/FALSE) abbreviation: the abbreviation of the party's name

the final file should be a csv file."

```{r AUTONOMICAL CANDIDATES 2000-2012 PP}
           str_squish(),

    is_titular,
```

# Municipal Elections


```{r READ ALL VOX MUNICIPAL CANDIDATES}
# municipality -> province, from the INE list (one sheet per province). The key
# ignores accents, case and the order of the bilingual halves, because the file
# writes "Alicante/Alacant" and the INE "Alacant/Alicante".
municipalities <- list()
for (s in excel_sheets("26codmun.xlsx")) {
  municipalities[[s]] <- read_excel("26codmun.xlsx", sheet = s, skip = 2,
                                    col_types = "text") |>
    filter(!is.na(CMUN)) |>
    transmute(province_code = CPRO, municipality = NOMBRE)
}
municipalities <- bind_rows(municipalities) |>
  left_join(provinces, by = "province_code") |>
  mutate(muni_key = municipality |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_split("/") |>
           map_chr(~ str_c(sort(str_squish(.x)), collapse = "/"))) |>
  distinct(muni_key, province)

municipal_vox <- readxl::read_xlsx("CANDIDATOS_MUNICIPALES.xlsx") |>
  mutate(muni_key = CIRCUNSCRIPCION |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_split("/") |>
           map_chr(~ str_c(sort(str_squish(.x)), collapse = "/"))) |>
  left_join(municipalities, by = "muni_key", relationship = "many-to-many")

# a municipality name shared by several provinces ("Villanueva", "Castrillo"...)
# duplicates the rows: keep the province that belongs to the list's region, taken
# from the names that are not shared
region_provinces <- municipal_vox |>
  group_by(ELECCION, CIRCUNSCRIPCION, ORDEN) |>
  filter(n() == 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  distinct(CCAA, province)

municipal_vox <- municipal_vox |>
  group_by(ELECCION, CIRCUNSCRIPCION, ORDEN) |>
  filter(n() == 1 | province %in% region_provinces$province[region_provinces$CCAA == first(CCAA)]) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  transmute(
    election      = ELECCION,
    year          = as.integer(str_extract(ELECCION, "\\d{4}")),
    chamber       = CIRCUNSCRIPCION,   # the municipality
    province,                          # its province, from the INE list
    list_position = as.integer(ORDEN),
    candidate     = CANDIDATO,
    is_elected    = ELEGIDO,
    source        = FUENTE,
    level         = "Municipal"
  )
# municipalities the INE list no longer carries under that name (it is dated
# 1 January 2026 and these data reach 2015), assigned by hand
manual_provinces <- tribble(
  ~chamber,                       ~province_manual,
  "Castell-Platja d'Aro",         "Girona",
  "Sant Carles de la Ràpita",     "Tarragona",
  "Moncada",                      "Valencia",
  "Alfarp",                       "Valencia",
  "Castelló de la Plana",         "Castellon",
  "Guadiana del Caudillo",        "Badajoz",
  "Maó-Mahón",                    "Illes Balears"
)

municipal_vox <- municipal_vox |>
  left_join(manual_provinces, by = "chamber") |>
  mutate(province = coalesce(province, province_manual)) |>
  select(-province_manual)
```

VER SI SOLO CONCURRIO EN 646 municipios de 8116 en 2019

```{r READ ALL PP MUNICIPAL CANDIDATES}
# PP candidates in the municipal elections. The ministry's file 04 for municipal
# elections carries the municipality, and up to 2003 the name is in one field, so
# read 26-100 as a single block: in the split layout the three fields are adjacent
# and str_squish collapses the padding to the same result.
PORTAL <- "https://infoelectoral.interior.gob.es/estaticos/docxl/apliextr"
dir.create("datos_pp_locales", showWarnings = FALSE)

cols_04_local <- fwf_cols(
  province_code  = c( 10,  11),
  muni_code      = c( 13,  15),   # 12 is a control digit
  party_code     = c( 16,  21),
  list_position  = c( 22,  24),
  candidate_type = c( 25,  25),
  full_name_cand = c( 26, 100),
  sex            = c(101, 101),
  elected        = c(120, 120)
)
latin1 <- locale(encoding = "ISO-8859-1")

# file 03: candidacies (parties)
cols_03 <- fwf_cols(
  party_code   = c(  9,  14),
  abbreviation = c( 15,  64),
  full_name    = c( 65, 214)
)

# municipality names, one sheet per province
municipalities <- list()
for (s in excel_sheets("26codmun.xlsx")) {
  municipalities[[s]] <- read_excel("26codmun.xlsx", sheet = s, skip = 2,
                                    col_types = "text")
}
municipalities <- bind_rows(municipalities) |>
  filter(!is.na(CMUN)) |>
  transmute(province_code = CPRO, muni_code = CMUN, municipality = NOMBRE)

local_candidates <- list()
years <- c("2003", "2007", "2011", "2015", "2019", "2023")

for (i in seq_along(years)) {

  folder   <- str_c("04", years[i], "05_TOTA")
  zip_file <- str_c("datos_pp_locales/", folder, ".zip")
  unzip_to <- tempfile()

  if (!file.exists(zip_file))
    download.file(str_c(PORTAL, "/", folder, ".zip"), zip_file, mode = "wb", quiet = TRUE)
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = unzip_to)

  path_03 <- list.files(unzip_to, "^03.*[.]DAT$", full.names = TRUE,
                        recursive = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]
  path_04 <- list.files(unzip_to, "^04.*[.]DAT$", full.names = TRUE,
                        recursive = TRUE, ignore.case = TRUE)[1]

  # the full name is the reliable filter: many local parties are abbreviated PPx
  # ("PPN" is Partido Progresista Nerjeño, "P.P.SO." Plataforma del Pueblo Soriano)
  parties <- read_fwf(path_03, cols_03, locale = latin1,
                      col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), str_trim)) |>
    filter(str_detect(stringi::stri_trans_general(str_to_upper(full_name),
                                                  "Latin-ASCII"),
                      "PARTIDO POPULAR|PARTIT POPULAR"))

  message("Reading municipal ", years[i], " ...")

  local_candidates[[i]] <- read_fwf(path_04, cols_04_local, locale = latin1,
                                    col_types = cols(.default = "c")) |>
    mutate(across(everything(), str_trim)) |>
    inner_join(parties, by = "party_code") |>
    mutate(year = years[i])
}

municipal_pp <- bind_rows(local_candidates) |>
  left_join(municipalities, by = c("province_code", "muni_code")) |>
  left_join(provinces, by = "province_code") |>
  transmute(
    election      = str_c("municipal_", year, "_05"),
    year          = as.integer(year),
    chamber       = municipality,
    province,
    list_position = as.integer(list_position),
    candidate     = str_squish(full_name_cand),
    sex           = recode(sex, "M" = "Male", "F" = "Female", .default = NA_character_),
    is_titular    = candidate_type == "T",
    is_elected    = elected == "S",
    abbreviation  = "PP",
    level         = "Municipal"
  ) |>
  arrange(year, province, chamber, list_position)
```

## Vox's Satellite organizations 

```{r VOX'S SATELLITE ORGANIZATION MEMBERS}

pages <- tribble(
  ~organisation, ~prefix,
  "DENAES",      "denaes.es/quienes-somos",
  "Disenso",     "fundaciondisenso.org/nosotros",
  "ISSEP",       "issep.es/nosotros",
  "ISSEP",       "issep.es/profesores",
  "HazteOir",    "hazteoir.org/conocenos",
  "HazteOir",    "www.hazteoir.org/conocenos",
  "CitizenGO",   "citizengo.org/es/conocenos",
  "CitizenGO",   "www.citizengo.org/es/conocenos",
  "CitizenGO",   "citizengo.org/en/about-us",
  "Solidaridad", "sindicatosolidaridad.es/contacto"
)

# --- 1. what the Archive has --------------------------------------------------
captures <- pages |>
  mutate(cdx = map(prefix, \(p)
    request("http://web.archive.org/cdx/search/cdx") |>
      req_url_query(url = p, matchType = "prefix", output = "json",
                    fl = "timestamp,original", collapse = "digest",
                    filter = c("statuscode:200", "mimetype:text/html"),
                    limit = 2000, .multi = "explode") |>
      req_retry(max_tries = 3) |>
      req_perform() |> resp_body_json() |>
      (\(x) tibble(timestamp = map_chr(x[-1], 1), original = map_chr(x[-1], 2)))())) |>
  unnest(cdx) |>
  mutate(date = ymd(str_sub(timestamp, 1, 8)), year = year(date),
         snapshot = str_c("https://web.archive.org/web/", timestamp, "id_/", original)) |>
  # one capture per page and year is enough to follow who is on a board
  slice_max(date, n = 1, by = c(original, year), with_ties = FALSE)

# --- 2. download them in parallel ---------------------------------------------
responses <- captures$snapshot |>
  map(\(u) request(u) |> req_timeout(30) |> req_error(is_error = \(r) FALSE)) |>
  req_perform_parallel(max_active = 5, on_error = "continue", progress = TRUE)

lines <- captures |>
  mutate(html = map_chr(responses, possibly(\(r) resp_body_string(r), NA_character_))) |>
  filter(!is.na(html)) |>
  # only the code is dropped. These sites wrap their content in <header> and
  # <aside>, so removing those takes the board away with the menu; the census
  # test below is what actually separates people from navigation.
  mutate(text = map(html, \(h) {
    page <- read_html(h)
    page |> html_elements("script, style, noscript") |> xml2::xml_remove()
    page |> html_elements("body") |> html_text2() |> str_split_1("\n") |> str_squish()
  }), .keep = "unused") |>
  unnest(text) |>
  filter(text != "")

# --- 3. which of those lines is a person --------------------------------------
PARTICLES <- c("de", "del", "la", "las", "los", "y", "e", "da", "do", "van", "von", "i")

# labels, menus and headlines the capitalisation rule would otherwise accept
NOT_A_PERSON <- str_c(
  "EQUIPO|CONSEJO|PATRONATO|DIRECCION|COMITE|JUNTA|FUNDACION|INSTITUTO|SINDICATO|",
  "ASOCIACION|UNIVERSIT|SCIENCES PO|COLLEGE|SCHOOL|REVISTA|DIARIO|DIGEST|OBJECTIVE|",
  "TELEVISION|NEWSLETTER|GACETA|BLOG|ESCUELA|CENTRO|OBSERVATORIO|PREMIO|PROGRAMA|",
  "CURSO|JORNADA|CONGRESO|ESPANA|NACIONAL|INTERNACIONAL|MOVIMIENTO|INICIO|CONTACTO|",
  "PRENSA|AGENDA|BOLETIN|TIENDA|AVISO|LEGAL|PRIVACIDAD|COOKIES|DISCURSO|ENTREVISTA|",
  "ARTICULO|CONFERENCIA|PONENCIA|VIDEO|FOUNDATION|CAMPAIGN|MANAGER|IP ADDRESS|",
  "SOBRE NOSOTROS|^LEER|^VER |^FISCAL|ENGLISH|ESPANOL|FRANCAIS|DEUTSCH|",
  "ISSEP|DISENSO|CITIZENGO|HAZTEOIR|DENAES")

# what may follow a name and be kept. The column is "role or description" on
# purpose: these sites print a post ("Presidente") and a profession
# ("Filosofo", "Pediatra") in exactly the same place
ROLES <- str_c(
  "PRESIDENT|VICEPRESIDENT|DIRECTOR|SECRETARI|TESORER|VOCAL|PATRON|COORDINADOR|",
  "RESPONSABLE|GERENTE|PORTAVOZ|FUNDADOR|MIEMBRO|ASESOR|PROFESOR|CATEDRATIC|",
  "DOCENTE|INVESTIGADOR|ANALISTA|CONSEJER|DELEGAD|ESCRITOR|PERIODISTA|FILOSOF|",
  "HISTORIADOR|ABOGAD|ECONOMISTA|MILITAR|EMPRESARI|MAGISTRAD|SOCIOLOG|POLITOLOG|",
  "JURISTA|DECANO|RECTOR|EDITOR|COLUMNISTA|DIPUTAD|SENADOR|EURODIPUTAD")

flat <- function(x) str_to_upper(stringi::stri_trans_general(x, "Latin-ASCII"))

# The real test of whether a line is a person: the INE census lists, which the
# project already uses to assign sex to candidates. A word list of things that
# are NOT names never ends; a list of the names that exist does.
ine_forenames <- c("Hombres", "Mujeres") |>
  map(\(s) read_excel("nombres_por_edad_media.xlsx", sheet = s, skip = 5)$Nombre) |>
  list_c() |> flat() |> str_squish()

# nicknames and rare forenames the census does not carry
ALSO_PEOPLE <- c("CAKE", "EDMALY")

# 2 to 6 words, all of them capitalised except the particles
is_person <- function(x) {
  capitalised <- map_lgl(str_split(x, " "), \(w) {
    w <- w[!str_to_lower(flat(w)) %in% PARTICLES]
    length(w) >= 2 && all(str_detect(w, "^\\p{Lu}\\p{L}"))
  })
  str_length(x) >= 5 & str_length(x) <= 60 &
    str_count(x, "\\S+") >= 2 & str_count(x, "\\S+") <= 6 &
    !str_detect(x, "[0-9@#/|]") & capitalised &
    flat(word(x, 1)) %in% c(ine_forenames, ALSO_PEOPLE) &
    !str_detect(flat(x), NOT_A_PERSON) & !str_detect(flat(x), ROLES)
}

people <- lines |>
  # "Ignacio Arsuaga Rato, Presidente" is a person and their role on one line;
  # without splitting it, the line is thrown away for containing "Presidente"
  separate_wider_delim(text, ", ", names = c("person", "inline_role"),
                       too_many = "merge", too_few = "align_start") |>
  mutate(inline_role = replace_na(inline_role, ""),
         # the other layout puts the role on the line below the name
         next_line = lead(person), .by = c(organisation, original, timestamp)) |>
  filter(is_person(person)) |>
  mutate(role = case_when(
           str_detect(flat(inline_role), ROLES) ~ inline_role,
           str_detect(flat(next_line), ROLES) & str_length(next_line) <= 90 ~ next_line,
           .default = ""),
         # Disenso prints the same board in caps on one page and in title case
         # on another: "AMANDO DE MIGUEL" and "Amando de Miguel" are one person
         person = if_else(person == str_to_upper(person), str_to_title(person), person),
         person = str_replace_all(person, str_c("(?<= )(", str_c(str_to_title(PARTICLES),
                                                                 collapse = "|"), ")(?= )"),
                                  str_to_lower))

# the same person is listed with and without the second surname ("Ana Velasco",
# "Ana Velasco Vidal-Abarca"): the longest form wins
variants <- people |>
  distinct(person) |>
  # compound surnames are opened at the hyphen, so that "Alejo Vidal Quadras"
  # falls inside "Alejo Vidal-Quadras Roca"
  mutate(tokens = str_split(flat(person), "[ -]"), first = map_chr(tokens, 1))

people <- variants |>
  rename(long = person, long_tokens = tokens) |>
  inner_join(rename(variants, short = person, short_tokens = tokens), by = "first",
             relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(map2_lgl(short_tokens, long_tokens, \(s, l) all(s %in% l)),
         lengths(short_tokens) <= lengths(long_tokens)) |>
  slice_max(lengths(long_tokens), n = 1, by = short, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(person = short, canonical = long) |>
  right_join(people, by = "person") |>
  mutate(person = coalesce(canonical, person)) |>
  summarise(.by = c(organisation, person),
            roles      = str_c(sort(unique(role[role != ""])), collapse = " | "),
            first_seen = min(date),
            last_seen  = max(date),
            n_captures = n_distinct(timestamp),
            source     = first(str_c("https://web.archive.org/web/", timestamp, "/", original))) |>
  arrange(organisation, person)

# --- 4. Solidaridad, from the BOE ---------------------------------------------
# The union's website archives no team page, so its officers are taken from the
# four announcements of the deposit of its statutes (Direccion General de
# Trabajo, union SPDSTE, deposit number 99105954). Searched at boe.es for
# SPDSTE in the title. Rafael Martinez de la Gandara, who signs all four, is
# the civil servant issuing the resolution and is NOT part of the union.
solidaridad_boe <- tribble(
  ~person,                              ~roles,             ~date,        ~boe,
  "Santiago Alarcón Gordon",            "Solicitante del depósito", "2020-08-12", "BOE-B-2020-26040",
  "Paula Bernardina Hidalgo de la Cruz","Promotora",        "2020-08-12", "BOE-B-2020-26040",
  "Raquel Moreno Barba",                "Promotora",        "2020-08-12", "BOE-B-2020-26040",
  "Ángel García Ochoa",                 "Promotor",         "2020-08-12", "BOE-B-2020-26040",
  "Santiago Alarcón Gordon",            "Solicitante del depósito", "2021-02-15", "BOE-B-2021-7089",
  "Rodrigo Alonso Fernández",           "Secretario General", "2021-02-15", "BOE-B-2021-7089",
  "Javier Tomás de la Cruz Bazo",       "Solicitante del depósito", "2025-05-23", "BOE-B-2025-18656",
  "Jordi Albert de la Fuente Miró",     "Secretario General", "2025-05-23", "BOE-B-2025-18656",
  "Javier Tomás de la Cruz Bazo",       "Solicitante del depósito", "2026-07-03", "BOE-B-2026-22639",
  "Jordi Albert de la Fuente Miró",     "Secretario General", "2026-07-03", "BOE-B-2026-22639"
) |>
  summarise(.by = person,
            organisation = "Solidaridad",
            roles      = str_c(sort(unique(roles)), collapse = " | "),
            first_seen = min(ymd(date)),
            last_seen  = max(ymd(date)),
            n_captures = n(),
            source     = str_c("https://www.boe.es/diario_boe/txt.php?id=", first(boe)))

people <- 
  bind_rows(people, solidaridad_boe) |> 
  arrange(organisation, person) |> 
   mutate(person = person |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_remove_all("[^A-Z ]") |>
           str_squish()) |> 
  filter(!person %in% c("ADOLFO SUAREZ", "YA SOMOS", "SEGUNDO APELLIDO"))

# --- 5. other organisations found in the press and Wikipedia ------------------
# organisations the candidates within the expected seats belonged to before
# (or besides) Vox: federations, foundations, associations, platforms
press_organisations <- read_excel("ORGANIZACIONES_CANDIDATOS_VOX.xlsx") |>
  select(person = PERSON_ID, organisation = ORGANIZACION, roles = ROL, source = FUENTE)

people <- people |>
  bind_rows(press_organisations) |>
  arrange(organisation, person)

# --- 6. Revuelta and Homo Legens, from the press ------------------------------
# Revuelta: youth association launched in October 2023 by five Vox affiliates and
# party employees, who formed its board; the board is the one reported when two of
# them took the association to the prosecutor over the DANA donations.
# Homo Legens: publishing house of the Intereconomia group, founded in 2017 by the
# former PP deputy Julio Ariza and run by his son Gabriel; it publishes the books of
# Vox leaders and has employed Lidia Bedman, Santiago Abascal's wife, since 2019
REVUELTA_SOURCE    <- "https://www.eldebate.com/espana/20251211/revuelta-asociacion-juvenil-denunciado-vox-claves-polemica_364072.html"
HOMO_LEGENS_SOURCE <- "https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homo_Legens"

press_satellites <- tribble(
  ~person,                      ~organisation, ~roles,
  "Jaime Hernández Zúñiga",     "Revuelta",    "Presidente",
  "Arturo Villarroya González", "Revuelta",    "Vicepresidente",
  "Pablo González Gasca",       "Revuelta",    "Secretario",
  "Javier Esteban Bejarano",    "Revuelta",    "Vocal",
  "Santiago Aneiros",           "Revuelta",    "Vocal | Tesorero de facto",
  "Julio Ariza",                "Homo Legens", "Fundador",
  "Gabriel Ariza",              "Homo Legens", "Director",
  "Kiko Méndez-Monasterio",     "Homo Legens", "Figura clave de la editorial",

) |>
  mutate(source = if_else(organisation == "Revuelta", REVUELTA_SOURCE, HOMO_LEGENS_SOURCE),
         person = person |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>

people <- people |>
```

```{r TABLE OF VOX'S SATELLITE ORGANIZATIONS}
# the organisations around Vox whose members were collected above, with how many of
# them could be identified and how many of those have stood on a Vox list. The
# organisations of step 5 (federations, foundations, associations the candidates
# belonged to before Vox) are not satellites and stay out of the table
satellite_organisations <- tribble(
  ~organisation, ~type,                     ~founded, ~link_with_vox,
  "DENAES",      "Foundation",              2006,     "Founded and chaired by Santiago Abascal before Vox",
  "HazteOir",    "Association (lobby)",     2001,     "Ultra-Catholic lobby, ally of Vox",
  "CitizenGO",   "Online platform",         2013,     "International platform of HazteOir",
  "Homo Legens", "Publishing house",        2017,     "Publisher of Vox leaders (Intereconomia group)",
  "Disenso",     "Foundation (think tank)", 2020,     "Think tank of Vox, chaired by Santiago Abascal",
  "ISSEP",       "Training institute",      2020,     "Madrid branch of Marion Marechal's institute; trains Vox cadres",
  "Solidaridad", "Trade union",             2020,     "Trade union promoted by Vox",
  "Revuelta",    "Youth association",       2023,     "Launched by Vox affiliates and employees"
)

satellite_members <- people |>
  filter(organisation %in% satellite_organisations$organisation) |>
  summarise(members        = n_distinct(person),
            vox_candidates = n_distinct(person[person %in% vox_candidates$person_id]),
            .by = organisation)

satellite_table <- satellite_organisations |>
  left_join(satellite_members, by = "organisation") |>
  mutate(across(c(members, vox_candidates), \(x) replace_na(x, 0L))) |>
  arrange(founded) |>
  # as text: stargazer prints numbers with a thousands separator ("2,006")
  mutate(founded = as.character(founded)) |>
  select(Organisation = organisation, Type = type, Founded = founded, `Link with Vox` = link_with_vox,
         `Members identified` = members, `Vox candidates` = vox_candidates)

stargazer(as.data.frame(satellite_table), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Vox's satellite organisations",
          notes = c("Members identified: board members and staff found in the archived websites (Wayback Machine),",
                    "the BOE (Solidaridad) and the press (Revuelta, Homo Legens). Vox candidates: members who stood on a Vox list."))

# who they are
people |>
  filter(organisation %in% satellite_organisations$organisation,
         person %in% vox_candidates$person_id) |>
  distinct(organisation, person, roles) |>
  arrange(organisation, person) |>
  print(n = Inf)
```

## Data Enrichment

```{r HARMONIZE SEX}
# every source writes sex its own way ("M"/"F", "Hombre"/"Mujer", "Male"/"Female")
# and the municipal lists do not carry it at all. Harmonised to Female/Male, and
# filled, in this order: 1. what the list says, 2. what the other lists of the same
# person say, 3. the forename, with the INE census of names

# 1. the forenames of the INE census, each with the sex of most of its holders
ine_forenames_sex <- bind_rows(
  read_excel("nombres_por_edad_media.xlsx", sheet = "Hombres", skip = 5) |> mutate(sex_forename = "Male"),
  read_excel("nombres_por_edad_media.xlsx", sheet = "Mujeres", skip = 5) |> mutate(sex_forename = "Female")) |>
  mutate(forename = Nombre |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_remove_all("[^A-Z ]") |>
           str_squish()) |>
  filter(!is.na(forename)) |>
  slice_max(Frecuencia, n = 1, by = forename, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(forename, sex_forename, frequency = Frecuencia) |>
  arrange(desc(frequency))

# 2. what each list says, harmonised ("MUJER" is checked before the "M" of Male)
vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  mutate(sex = case_when(str_detect(str_to_upper(sex), "^(F|MUJER|FEMALE|FEMENINO)") ~ "Female",
                         str_detect(str_to_upper(sex), "^(M|H|MALE|HOMBRE|MASCULINO|VARON)") ~ "Male"))

# 3. the sex the person has in their other lists
sex_by_person <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(!is.na(sex)) |>
  count(person_id, sex) |>
  slice_max(n, n = 1, by = person_id, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(person_id, sex_person = sex)

# 4. the sex of the forename, trying in this order:
#    a. the first two words ("MARIA JOSE", "JOSE MARIA"); "M"/"MA" stand for Maria
#    b. the first word
#    c. forenames written together ("JUANCARLOS", "MARIAJESUS"): the longest census
#       forename the first word starts with
#    d. the second forename, skipping particles ("LEONIA ALEXANDRA", "J DEL ROCIO")
#    e. foreign or rare forenames the census does not carry, set by hand below
#    f. a misspelt first word ("PACUAL", "MAGADALENA"): the census forename one letter apart
#    g. what is left: ending in -A, Female; otherwise, Male
census_forenames <- ine_forenames_sex |>
  filter(frequency >= 100, !str_detect(forename, " "))

forename_corrections <- tribble(
  ~first_one,     ~sex_e,
  "ANABEIDY",     "Female", "ANATERESA",  "Female", "ANAVANESA",  "Female", "AHIATIMA",   "Female",
  "AUVELLY",      "Female", "CARUCHA",    "Female", "DOBROSLAVA", "Female", "EMERENCIA",  "Female",
  "EUDIVIGIS",    "Female", "EUKARIS",    "Female", "FAITIA",     "Female", "GLISELIA",   "Female",
  "IBOLYAKINGA",  "Female", "ISOLGITA",   "Female", "LUCIVANIA",  "Female", "MAGACEDA",   "Female",
  "MALLAURY",     "Female", "MARIUXI",    "Female", "MERCHINES",  "Female", "MISSANDRA",  "Female",
  "NAOULA",       "Female", "OSDANAY",    "Female", "OSLAIDA",    "Female", "SLADANA",    "Female",
  "VALBONA",      "Female", "YULEISIS",   "Female", "IDERMIS",    "Female", "ENERIET",    "Female",
  "ARGYRIS",      "Male",   "BEDROS",     "Male",   "CANCIANO",   "Male",   "CESIDIO",    "Male",
  "GARBEIL",      "Male",   "HARTIOUN",   "Male",   "KEFAH",      "Male",   "OLIVEIRO",   "Male",
  "SANTE",        "Male",   "SIQUEM",     "Male",   "TRAJANO",    "Male",   "TROYANO",    "Male",
  "VANGELIS",     "Male",   "AMROU",      "Male"
)

sex_by_forename <- vox_candidates |>
  distinct(person_id) |>
  mutate(name      = str_replace(person_id, "^MA? ", "MARIA "),
         first_two = word(name, 1, 2),
         first_one = word(name, 1),
         second    = word(str_squish(str_remove_all(name, "\\b(DE|DEL|LA|LAS|LOS)\\b")), 2)) |>
  left_join(ine_forenames_sex |> select(first_two = forename, sex_a = sex_forename), by = "first_two") |>
  left_join(ine_forenames_sex |> select(first_one = forename, sex_b = sex_forename), by = "first_one") |>
  left_join(ine_forenames_sex |> select(second = forename, sex_d = sex_forename), by = "second")

written_together <- sex_by_forename |>
  filter(is.na(sex_a), is.na(sex_b)) |>
  distinct(first_one) |>
  cross_join(census_forenames |> filter(str_length(forename) >= 4) |> select(forename, sex_forename)) |>
  filter(str_starts(first_one, forename), first_one != forename) |>
  slice_max(str_length(forename), n = 1, by = first_one, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  select(first_one, sex_c = sex_forename)

misspelt <- sex_by_forename |>
  filter(is.na(sex_a), is.na(sex_b), is.na(sex_d)) |>
  distinct(first_one)

distances <- adist(misspelt$first_one, census_forenames$forename)

misspelt <- misspelt |>
  mutate(closest  = census_forenames$forename[apply(distances, 1, which.min)],
         distance = apply(distances, 1, min),
         sex_f    = if_else(distance == 1, census_forenames$sex_forename[apply(distances, 1, which.min)], NA))

sex_by_forename <- sex_by_forename |>
  left_join(written_together, by = "first_one") |>
  left_join(misspelt |> select(first_one, closest, sex_f), by = "first_one") |>
  left_join(forename_corrections, by = "first_one") |>
  mutate(sex_g    = if_else(str_ends(first_one, "A"), "Female", "Male"),
         sex_name = coalesce(sex_a, sex_b, sex_c, sex_d, sex_e, sex_f, sex_g),
         sex_rule = case_when(!is.na(sex_a) ~ "a", !is.na(sex_b) ~ "b", !is.na(sex_c) ~ "c",
                              !is.na(sex_d) ~ "d", !is.na(sex_e) ~ "e", !is.na(sex_f) ~ "f", TRUE ~ "g"))

# names resolved by the weaker rules (f, g): check them
sex_by_forename |> filter(sex_rule %in% c("f", "g")) |> select(person_id, closest, sex_name, sex_rule) |> print(n = Inf)

sex_by_forename <- sex_by_forename |>
  select(person_id, sex_name)

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of(c("sex_person", "sex_name"))) |>
  left_join(sex_by_person, by = "person_id") |>
  left_join(sex_by_forename, by = "person_id") |>
  mutate(sex = coalesce(sex, sex_person, sex_name)) |>
  select(-sex_person, -sex_name)

count(vox_candidates, sex)

# names still without sex: must return 0 rows
vox_candidates |> filter(is.na(sex)) |> distinct(person_id)
```

```{r SIGNEES AND FOUNDERS}
# is_signee: signed the manifesto of reconversion.es; is_founder: in the founders table.
# As with the party organs, a name is found when its words are in the candidate's
# name; when it fits several candidates, the rule below picks one or leaves it out
reference_names <- bind_rows(
  signees_reconversion |> mutate(group = "signee"),
  founders |> select(name) |> mutate(group = "founder")) |>
  mutate(name_id = name |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_remove_all("[^A-Z ]") |>
           str_squish()) |>
  distinct(group, name_id)

reference_words <- reference_names |>
  distinct(name_id) |>
  mutate(word = name_id) |>
  separate_longer_delim(word, " ") |>
  distinct() |>
  add_count(name_id, name = "n_words")

candidate_words <- vox_candidates |>
  distinct(person_id) |>
  mutate(word = person_id) |>
  separate_longer_delim(word, " ") |>
  distinct()

# Vox elections and national or regional lists of each candidate, to break ties
candidate_record <- vox_candidates |>
  group_by(person_id) |>
  summarise(n_elections       = n_distinct(election),
            national_regional = any(level != "Municipal"),
            .groups = "drop")

reference_matches <- reference_words |>
  filter(n_words >= 2) |>
  inner_join(candidate_words, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(name_id, person_id, n_words, name = "words_found") |>
  filter(words_found == n_words,
         # the words in the same order and together, except a middle name after the
         # first one: "Pedro Fernandez Barbadillo" is "Pedro Maria Fernandez Barbadillo",
         # but "Enrique Alvarez Lopez" is not "Enrique Lopez Alvarez" and
         # "Jose Maria Alvarez" is not "Jose Maria Figaredo Alvarez Sala"
         str_detect(person_id, str_c("\\b", word(name_id, 1), "\\b(.* )?", word(name_id, 2, -1), "\\b"))) |>
  left_join(candidate_record, by = "person_id") |>
  add_count(name_id, name = "n_candidates")

# names that fit several candidates ("Santiago Abascal": Abascal Conde and his father
# Abascal Escuza): the one who ran in national or regional lists in more elections
chosen <- reference_matches |>
  filter(n_candidates == 1 | national_regional) |>
  slice_max(n_elections, n = 1, by = name_id) |>
  add_count(name_id, name = "n_chosen") |>
  filter(n_chosen == 1)

# the same person under a shorter name ("Ana Velasco Vidalabarca" and
# "Ana Maria Velasco Vidalabarca") is kept as well
same_person <- reference_matches |>
  inner_join(chosen |> select(name_id, chosen_id = person_id), by = "name_id") |>
  filter(person_id != chosen_id,
         map2_lgl(str_split(person_id, " "), str_split(chosen_id, " "), \(p, c) all(p %in% c)))

# names left out: check them by hand
reference_matches |> filter(!name_id %in% chosen$name_id) |> arrange(name_id)

matched <- reference_names |>
  inner_join(bind_rows(chosen, same_person) |> select(name_id, person_id), by = "name_id",
             relationship = "many-to-many")   # a founder can also be a signee

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  mutate(is_signee  = person_id %in% matched$person_id[matched$group == "signee"],
         is_founder = person_id %in% matched$person_id[matched$group == "founder"])
```

```{r VOX CER MEMBERS y NO SE QUE OTRA COSA}
# one row per organic position, CEN flagged
vox_positions <- read_excel("VOX_CARGOS_ORGANOS.xlsx", sheet = "01 Personas y cargos") |>
  mutate(name       = Nombre,
         position   = Cargo,
         organ      = Organo,
         first_seen = ymd(`Primera constancia`),
         last_seen  = ymd(`Ultima constancia`),
         in_cen     = str_detect(Organo, "^CEN|^Comite Ejecutivo Nacional"),
         name_id    = name |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_remove_all("[^A-Z ]") |>
           str_squish()) |>
  select(name, name_id, position, organ, first_seen, last_seen, in_cen)

# the organs give short names ("Alejandro Nolasco"), the lists full ones
# ("Alejandro Nolasco Asensio"): a name matches a candidate when all its words
# are in the candidate's name, and only if exactly one candidate fits
name_words <- vox_positions |>
  distinct(name_id) |>
  mutate(word = name_id) |>
  separate_longer_delim(word, " ") |>
  distinct() |>
  add_count(name_id, name = "n_words")

candidate_words <- vox_candidates |>
  distinct(person_id) |>
  mutate(word = person_id) |>
  separate_longer_delim(word, " ") |>
  distinct()

name_matches <- name_words |>
  inner_join(candidate_words, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  count(name_id, person_id, n_words, name = "words_found") |>
  filter(words_found == n_words) |>
  add_count(name_id, name = "n_candidates")

# names that fit several candidates: left out, check them by hand
name_matches |> filter(n_candidates > 1) |> arrange(name_id)

# last capture of the VOX website: whoever still appears then is still in the CEN
last_capture <- ymd("2026-09-06")

organ_info <- vox_positions |>
  inner_join(name_matches |> filter(n_candidates == 1) |> select(name_id, person_id), by = "name_id") |>
  group_by(person_id) |>
  summarise(organic_positions = str_c(unique(position), collapse = " | "),
            organ_first_seen  = first(sort(first_seen)),
            organ_last_seen   = last(sort(last_seen)),
            cen_from          = first(sort(first_seen[in_cen])),
            cen_to            = last(sort(last_seen[in_cen])),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(cen_to = if_else(cen_to == last_capture, NA, cen_to))   # NA = still in the CEN

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of(c("organic_positions", "organ_first_seen", "organ_last_seen", "in_cen", "cen_from", "cen_to",
                   "has_organic_position", "in_cen_at_election", "in_cen_before"))) |>
  left_join(organ_info, by = "person_id") |>
  mutate(has_organic_position = !is.na(organic_positions),
         # was in the CEN before this election (election month taken as its date)
         in_cen_before        = coalesce(cen_from < ym(str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}")), FALSE))
```

```{r SEATS ACTUALLY WON}
# seats Vox won in each list: one list = election + chamber + constituency
# (chamber keeps Congress and Senate apart; in municipal lists chamber is the municipality)
seats_won <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  group_by(election, chamber, province) |>
  summarise(seats_won = sum(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# did the number 1 of this same list (same chamber and constituency) win a seat
# in the previous election of that type? Whoever it was: not matched by name
previous_head_won <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA), list_position == 1) |>
  mutate(date = str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}")) |>
  group_by(chamber, province, date) |>
  summarise(head_won = any(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(chamber, province, date) |>
  group_by(chamber, province) |>
  mutate(previous_head_won = lag(head_won, default = FALSE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(chamber, province, date, previous_head_won)

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of(c("seats_won", "top_won"))) |>
  mutate(date = str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}")) |>
  left_join(seats_won,         by = c("election", "chamber", "province")) |>
  left_join(previous_head_won, by = c("chamber", "province", "date")) |>
  # top_won: heads this list, and the head of this list won a seat last time
  mutate(top_won = is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA) & list_position == 1 & previous_head_won %in% TRUE) |>
  select(-previous_head_won)
```

```{r VOX EXPECTED SEATS + TOP CANDIDATES}
# ---------------------------------------- 1. CIS estimate for each list (midpoint, rounded up)
# how the CIS spells the provinces that the lists spell differently
same_place <- c("ILLES BALEARS" = "BALEARES",
                "GIPUZKOA"      = "GUIPUZCOA",
                "BIZKAIA"       = "VIZCAYA",
                "ARABA/ALAVA"   = "ALAVA",
                "S.C. TENERIFE" = "SANTA CRUZ DE TENERIFE",
                "CIUDAD"        = "CIUDAD REAL")

cis_seats <- read_csv("cis_estimaciones_vox.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) |>
  mutate(date       = str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}"),
         # type of election of each estimate (the CIS does not estimate the Senate)
         cis_chamber = case_when(str_starts(election, "generales")   ~ "Congress",
                                 str_starts(election, "europeas")    ~ "European Parliament",
                                 str_starts(election, "autonomicas") ~ "Autonomical",
                                 str_starts(election, "municipales") ~ "Municipal"),
         place      = coalesce(province, circumscription) |>
                        str_to_upper() |>
                        stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII"),
         cis_seats  = ceiling((min_seats + max_seats) / 2),
         # the file also carries rows that are not CIS estimates
         cis_source = case_when(str_starts(source, "CIS")     ~ "CIS constituency estimate",
                                str_starts(source, "electos") ~ "previous result, same constituency",
                                TRUE                          ~ "no CIS estimate before 2018 (0)")) |>
  add_count(date, cis_chamber, place) |>
  filter(n == 1) |>                  # two municipalities called Cieza: no way to tell them apart
  select(date, cis_chamber, place, cis_seats, cis_source)

# ------------------ 2. fallback: seats won in that same list in the previous election
previous_seats <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  mutate(date = str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}")) |>
  group_by(chamber, province, date) |>
  summarise(seats_won = sum(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(chamber, province, date) |>
  group_by(chamber, province) |>
  mutate(previous_seats = lag(seats_won)) |>          # NA = first time Vox ran this list
  ungroup() |>
  select(chamber, province, date, previous_seats)

# ----------------------------------------------- 3. expected seats into the lists
vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of(c("expected_seats", "expected_seats_source", "top_expected"))) |>
  mutate(date        = str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}"),
         cis_chamber = case_when(chamber %in% c("Congress", "European Parliament") ~ chamber,
                                 level %in% c("Autonomical", "Municipal")          ~ level,
                                 TRUE                                              ~ "Senate"),
         place       = if_else(level == "Municipal", chamber, province) |>
                         str_to_upper() |>
                         stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII"),
         place       = if_else(chamber == "European Parliament", "ESPANA", place),
         place       = coalesce(same_place[place], place)) |>
  left_join(cis_seats,      by = c("date", "cis_chamber", "place")) |>
  left_join(previous_seats, by = c("chamber", "province", "date")) |>
  mutate(expected_seats        = coalesce(cis_seats, previous_seats, 0),
         expected_seats_source = case_when(!is.na(cis_seats)      ~ cis_source,
                                           !is.na(previous_seats) ~ "previous result, same constituency",
                                           TRUE                   ~ "first contest (0)"),
         top_expected          = is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA) & list_position <= expected_seats) |>
  select(-cis_chamber, -place, -cis_seats, -cis_source, -previous_seats)

# ---------------- 4. did the person win a seat in the election they ran in just before?
seat_by_date <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(!is.na(person_id), person_id != "") |>
  group_by(person_id, date) |>
  summarise(won_seat = any(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(person_id, date) |>
  group_by(person_id) |>
  mutate(had_seat_before = lag(won_seat, default = FALSE)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(person_id, date, had_seat_before)

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of("had_seat_before")) |>
  left_join(seat_by_date, by = c("person_id", "date")) |>
  mutate(had_seat_before = coalesce(had_seat_before, FALSE))
```

```{r PREV PARTY VARIABLE}
# ------------------------------------ 2. every candidacy for another party, with its year
other_party_candidacies <- bind_rows(
  pp_candidates |> mutate(prev_party = "PP") |> select(person_id, year, prev_party),
  cs_candidates |> mutate(prev_party = "Cs") |> select(person_id, year, prev_party),
  radical_right_candidates |>
    left_join(party_abbreviations, by = "party") |>
    select(person_id, year, prev_party)) |>
  filter(!is.na(person_id), person_id != "") |>
  mutate(year = as.integer(year),
         person_id = person_id |>
           # labels the bulletins print after the name ("IND" for independents, the
           # party, the section), which stop the same person from matching
           str_remove(" (CV BOCYLD |TITULARES )?NUM$") |>
           str_remove(" (IND|JN|AND|UPN|FN|MOVIMENT SOCIAL)$") |>
           # surnames split at the end of the line in the PDFs: "FERNAND EZ"
           str_replace("(?<=[A-Z]{3}) (EZ|Z)$", "\\1") |>
           str_squish()) |>
  distinct()

# ------------------------------------ 3. parties found in the press (PREV_PARTY_PRENSA_VOX.xlsx):
# candidates within the expected seats who had been in another party before joining Vox
press_prev_party <- read_excel("PREV_PARTY_PRENSA_VOX.xlsx") |>
  select(person_id = PERSON_ID, prev_party = PARTIDO_ANTERIOR) |>
  separate_longer_delim(prev_party, " | ")

# ------------------- 4. parties the person had been in BEFORE each Vox candidacy
vox_candidacy_years <- vox_candidates |>
  distinct(person_id, year)

prev_party_by_year <- bind_rows(
  # ran for another party in an earlier year
  vox_candidacy_years |>
    inner_join(other_party_candidacies, by = "person_id", suffix = c("", "_other"),
               relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    filter(year_other < year) |>
    select(person_id, year, prev_party),
  # member of another party before joining Vox, according to the press
  vox_candidacy_years |>
    inner_join(press_prev_party, by = "person_id", relationship = "many-to-many")) |>
  group_by(person_id, year) |>
  summarise(prev_party = str_c(sort(unique(prev_party)), collapse = " | "), .groups = "drop")

vox_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  select(-any_of(c("prev_party", "has_prev_party"))) |>
  left_join(prev_party_by_year, by = c("person_id", "year")) |>
    mutate(has_prev_party = if_else(!is.na(prev_party), TRUE, NA))
```

```{r TABLE VOX RESULTS}
# one row per election: general elections keep Congress and Senate apart,
# regional elections held on the same day are counted together
vox_results <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  mutate(contest = if_else(level == "National", str_c(election, " ", chamber), election)) |>
  group_by(level, date, contest) |>
  summarise(lists            = n_distinct(chamber, province),
            candidates       = n(),

  arrange(factor(level, levels = c("National", "Autonomical", "Municipal")), date) |>
  select(Level = level, Election = contest, Lists = lists, Candidates = candidates,
         `Expected seats` = expected_seats, `Seats won` = seats_won, `Lists with seats` = lists_with_seats)

stargazer(as.data.frame(vox_results), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Vox electoral results by election",
```

```{r FACETED CARTOGRAM MAP}
library(mapSpain)
library(sf)
library(readxl)
library(cartogram)

# Vox's vote and its access to regional government in the four phases of the party, on
# a contiguous cartogram (r-graph-gallery.com/331-basic-cartogram). Each region is
# resized by its area times Vox's vote share there: the total size of Spain does not
# change, and a region grows where Vox did better than its own average and shrinks where
# it did worse. The size compares Vox with itself, not with the other parties
phases <- tribble(
  ~phase,       ~phase_start,       ~phase_end,
  "2014-2017",  ymd("2014-01-01"),  ymd("2017-12-31"),
  "2018-2019",  ymd("2018-01-01"),  ymd("2019-12-31"),
  "2020-2022",  ymd("2020-01-01"),  ymd("2022-12-31"),
  "2023-2026",  ymd("2023-01-01"),  ymd("2026-12-31")
)

# ---- 1. Vox's vote share by region in the general elections of each phase -------------
# Congress results by constituency (Ministry of the Interior, infoelectoral, PROV_02 files).
# There was no general election in 2020-2022: that phase keeps the result of November
# 2019, the one in force during it
general_by_phase <- tribble(
  ~file,                   ~phase,       ~election,
  "PROV_02_201512_1.zip",  "2014-2017",  "December 2015",
  "PROV_02_201606_1.zip",  "2014-2017",  "June 2016",
  "PROV_02_201904_1.zip",  "2018-2019",  "April 2019",
  "PROV_02_201911_1.zip",  "2018-2019",  "November 2019",
  "PROV_02_201911_1.zip",  "2020-2022",  "November 2019",
  "PROV_02_202307_1.zip",  "2023-2026",  "July 2023"
)

# the party names are in row 2 or 3 of each file and the column labels in row 4; the
# provinces start in row 5. Where Vox did not run, its votes are empty (0 votes)
general_results <- tibble(file = unique(general_by_phase$file)) |>
  mutate(results = map(file, \(f) {
    raw   <- read_excel(unzip(f, exdir = tempdir()), col_names = FALSE, col_types = "text")
    vox   <- which(unlist(raw[2, ]) == "VOX" | unlist(raw[3, ]) == "VOX")[1]
    valid <- which(unlist(raw[4, ]) == "Votos válidos")
    rows  <- which(str_detect(raw[[2]], "^[0-9]+$"))
    tibble(cpro        = str_pad(raw[[2]][rows], 2, pad = "0"),
           vox_votes   = replace_na(as.numeric(raw[[vox]][rows]), 0),
           valid_votes = as.numeric(raw[[valid]][rows]))
  })) |>
  unnest(results)

# 52 constituencies in every file (must return 0 rows)
general_results |> count(file) |> filter(n != 52)

# provinces added up to regions, and the elections of each phase averaged
vote_by_phase <- general_by_phase |>
  left_join(general_results, by = "file", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  left_join(esp_codelist |> distinct(cpro, codauto), by = "cpro") |>
  summarise(vote_share = 100 * sum(vox_votes) / sum(valid_votes), .by = c(phase, election, codauto)) |>
  summarise(vote_share = mean(vote_share), .by = c(phase, codauto))

# ---- 2. Vox in the regional government, or propping up a PP government --------------
# a Vox post counts in a phase if it started before the phase ended and ended after it
# started (posts still held have no end date)
vox_in_government <- vox_executive_positions |>
  mutate(start = dmy(start_date), end = coalesce(dmy(end_date), today())) |>
  left_join(tribble(~region,                 ~codauto,
                    "Andalucía",             "01",
                    "Aragón",                "02",
                    "Castilla y León",       "07",
                    "Comunidad Valenciana",  "10",
                    "Extremadura",           "11",
                    "Región de Murcia",      "14"), by = "region") |>
  cross_join(phases) |>
  filter(start <= phase_end, end >= phase_start) |>
  distinct(codauto, phase)

# PP governments that owed their investiture to the votes of Vox without Vox entering
# them, in office at some point of the phase
pp_needs_vox <- tribble(
  ~codauto, ~phase,       ~investiture,
  "01",     "2018-2019",  "Juan Manuel Moreno, January 2019 (PP-Cs)",
  "13",     "2018-2019",  "Isabel Díaz Ayuso, August 2019 (PP-Cs)",
  "14",     "2018-2019",  "Fernando López Miras, July 2019 (PP-Cs)",
  "01",     "2020-2022",  "Juan Manuel Moreno, in office until July 2022",
  "13",     "2020-2022",  "Isabel Díaz Ayuso, in office until 2021 and invested again with Vox votes in June 2021",
  "14",     "2020-2022",  "Fernando López Miras, in office until 2023",
  "04",     "2023-2026",  "Marga Prohens, July 2023"
)

# ---- 3. one contiguous cartogram per phase ----------------------------------------------
# equal-area projection (the cartogram works with areas); the Canary Islands are moved
# next to the peninsula before the calculation
regions <- esp_get_ccaa(epsg = "3035") |>
  select(codauto) |>
  mutate(area = as.numeric(st_area(geometry)))

# weight = area x vote share relative to Vox's national share in the phase. A region
# where Vox did not run keeps 5% of its size (a weight of zero cannot be drawn)
vox_cartogram <- phases$phase |>
  map(\(p) regions |>
        left_join(filter(vote_by_phase, phase == p), by = "codauto") |>
        mutate(phase    = p,
               relative = vote_share / weighted.mean(vote_share, area),
               weight   = area * pmax(relative, 0.05)) |>
        cartogram_cont("weight", itermax = 15)) |>
  bind_rows() |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
           str_c(codauto, phase) %in% str_c(vox_in_government$codauto, vox_in_government$phase) ~ "Vox in the government",
           str_c(codauto, phase) %in% str_c(pp_needs_vox$codauto, pp_needs_vox$phase)           ~ "PP government that needed Vox's votes",
           TRUE                                                                                  ~ "Neither") |>
           factor(levels = c("Vox in the government", "PP government that needed Vox's votes", "Neither")))

# ---- 4. the map ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# national vote share in each phase, for the panel titles
phase_names <- general_by_phase |>
  left_join(general_results, by = "file", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  summarise(vote_share = 100 * sum(vox_votes) / sum(valid_votes), .by = c(phase, election)) |>
  summarise(label = str_c(first(phase), "\n", str_c(election, collapse = " and "), ": ",
                          str_c(format(round(vote_share, 1), nsmall = 1), "%", collapse = " and ")),
            .by = phase) |>
  deframe()

ggplot(vox_cartogram) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = status), colour = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Vox in the government"                 = "#1b7a3d",
                               "PP government that needed Vox's votes" = "#9fd3ad",
                               "Neither"                               = "grey70"),
                    drop = FALSE, name = NULL) +
  facet_wrap(~ phase, ncol = 2, labeller = as_labeller(phase_names)) +
  labs(title = "Vox's vote and its access to regional government",
       subtitle = "Regions resized by Vox's vote there: larger where Vox did better than its own average",
       caption = str_c("Size: area of the region times Vox's share of the valid vote in the general elections of the phase,\n",
                       "relative to its national share (a region where Vox did not run keeps 5% of its size).\n",
                       "Colour: Vox held a post in the regional government, or its votes were needed to invest a PP president,\n",
                       "at any point of the phase. Source: Ministry of the Interior (infoelectoral). Canary Islands moved next to the peninsula.")) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(text = element_text(colour = "#22211d"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f5f4", colour = NA),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f5f4", colour = NA),
        legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#f5f5f4", colour = NA),
        plot.title = element_text(size = 16, hjust = 0.5, colour = "#4e4d47"),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 9, hjust = 0.5, colour = "#4e4d47", margin = margin(b = 8)),
        plot.caption = element_text(size = 7, hjust = 0, colour = "grey40"),
        strip.text = element_text(size = 9, margin = margin(b = 4)),
        legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.text = element_text(size = 8),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 10, 10, 10))
```

```{r MAP COUNCILLERS PRE 2018}
library(mapSpain)
library(sf)

# Vox councillors elected in the 2015 municipal elections (Vox's only local seats before 2018)
councillors_2015 <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(level == "Municipal", year == 2015, is_elected %in% TRUE) |>
  count(province, chamber, name = "councillors") |>
  mutate(muni_key = chamber |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_split("/") |>
           map_chr(\(x) str_c(sort(str_squish(x)), collapse = "/")))

municipalities_map <- esp_get_munic(epsg = "3857") |>
  left_join(provinces, by = c("cpro" = "province_code")) |>
  mutate(muni_key = name |>
           str_to_upper() |>
           stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |>
           str_split("/") |>
           map_chr(\(x) str_c(sort(str_squish(x)), collapse = "/")))

councillors_map <- municipalities_map |>
  inner_join(councillors_2015, by = c("muni_key", "province"))

# councillors whose municipality was not found on the map (must return 0 rows)
councillors_2015 |> anti_join(st_drop_geometry(councillors_map), by = c("muni_key", "province"))

# one point per municipality, at its centroid
councillors_centroids <- st_centroid(councillors_map)

councillors_points <- councillors_centroids |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  bind_cols(as_tibble(st_coordinates(councillors_centroids)))

ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = esp_get_prov(epsg = "3857"), fill = "grey95", colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_sf(data = esp_get_can_box(epsg = "3857"), colour = "grey60") +
  geom_point(data = councillors_points, aes(X, Y, size = councillors), colour = "#009E73") +
  ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = councillors_points, aes(X, Y, label = str_c(name, " (", councillors, ")")),
                           size = 3, min.segment.length = 0) +
  scale_size_continuous(range = c(2, 5), breaks = 1:3, name = "Councillors") +
  labs(title = "Vox councillors before 2018",
       subtitle = "Municipal elections of May 2015") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```


```{r TABLE VOX CANDIDATES BY LEVELS}
# profile of the candidates at each level (one row per candidacy)
candidates_by_level <- vox_candidates |>
  mutate(level = factor(level, levels = c("National", "Autonomical", "Municipal"))) |>
  group_by(level) |>
  summarise(`Candidacies`                        = n(),
            `Different people`                   = n_distinct(person_id),
            `Elections`                          = n_distinct(election),
            `Women (%)`                          = round(100 * mean(sex[!is.na(sex)] == "Female"), 1),
            `Elected (%)`                        = round(100 * mean(is_elected %in% TRUE), 1),
            `Within expected seats (%)`          = round(100 * mean(top_expected), 1),
            `Seat in previous election (%)`      = round(100 * mean(had_seat_before), 1),
            # has_prev_party is TRUE or NA: the NA count as no party on record
            `Ran for another party before (%)`   = round(100 * mean(has_prev_party %in% TRUE), 1),
            `In the CEN before the election (%)` = round(100 * mean(in_cen_before), 2),
            `Organic position in Vox (%)`        = round(100 * mean(has_organic_position), 2),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(level = as.character(level)) |>
  pivot_longer(-level, names_to = "Variable") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = level, values_from = value)

stargazer(as.data.frame(candidates_by_level), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Vox candidates by level of election",
          notes = "One row per candidacy. Sex of municipal candidates inferred from the forename (INE census).")

# the same variables for the candidates within the expected seats and the rest
candidates_by_expected <- vox_candidates |>
  mutate(group = if_else(top_expected, "Within expected seats", "Rest of the list")) |>
  group_by(group) |>
  summarise(`Candidacies`                        = n(),
            `Women (%)`                          = round(100 * mean(sex[!is.na(sex)] == "Female"), 1),
            `Elected (%)`                        = round(100 * mean(is_elected %in% TRUE), 1),
            `Seat in previous election (%)`      = round(100 * mean(had_seat_before), 1),
            `Ran for another party before (%)`   = round(100 * mean(has_prev_party %in% TRUE), 1),
            `In the CEN before the election (%)` = round(100 * mean(in_cen_before), 2),
            `Mean list position`                 = round(mean(list_position, na.rm = TRUE), 1),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "Variable") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = group, values_from = value)

stargazer(as.data.frame(candidates_by_expected), summary = FALSE, rownames = FALSE, type = table_type,
          title = "Candidates within and outside the expected seats")
```

```{r TERRITORIAL PENETRATION IN AUTONOMICAL ELECTIONS}
library(mapSpain)
library(sf)

# regional constituencies that are not provinces: islands, districts, regional lists
constituency_to_province <- tribble(
  ~province_key,                ~province_code,
  "REGION DE MURCIA",           "30",
  "PRIMERA",                    "30",
  "SEGUNDA",                    "30",
  "TERCERA",                    "30",
  "CUARTA",                     "30",
  "QUINTA",                     "30",
  "CENTRO",                     "33",
  "OCCIDENTE",                  "33",
  "ORIENTE",                    "33",
  "MALLORCA",                   "07",
  "MENORCA",                    "07",
  "EIVISSA",                    "07",
  "FORMENTERA",                 "07",
  "GRAN CANARIA",               "35",
  "LANZAROTE",                  "35",
  "FUERTEVENTURA",              "35",
  "TENERIFE",                   "38",
  "LA PALMA",                   "38",
  "LA GOMERA",                  "38",
  "EL HIERRO",                  "38",
  "CIRCUNSCRIPCION AUTONOMICA", "35",
  "CIRCUNSCRIPCION AUTONOMICA", "38",
  "CIUDAD",                     "13",   # "Ciudad Real" cut in the source
  "ALAVA",                      "01"
) |>
  bind_rows(provinces |>
              mutate(province_key = province |> str_to_upper() |> stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII")) |>
              select(province_key, province_code))

# ------------------------------- provinces that voted in each regional election
regional_lists <- autonomical_candidates |>
  filter(year >= 2014) |>
  mutate(province_key = province |> str_to_upper() |> stringi::stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") |> str_squish()) |>
  left_join(constituency_to_province, by = "province_key", relationship = "many-to-many")

# constituencies that could not be placed in a province (must return 0 rows)
regional_lists |> filter(is.na(province_code)) |> distinct(chamber, province)

regional_elections <- regional_lists |>
  distinct(election, cpro = province_code) |>
  left_join(esp_codelist |> distinct(cpro, ccaa = ccaa.shortname.es), by = "cpro") |>
  group_by(election) |>
  mutate(election_label = str_c(str_replace(str_extract(election, "[0-9]{4}_[0-9]{2}"), "_", "-"), "\n",
                                if_else(n_distinct(ccaa) == 1, first(ccaa), str_c(n_distinct(ccaa), " regions")))) |>
  ungroup()

vox_regional <- regional_lists |>
  filter(abbreviation == "VOX") |>
  distinct(election, cpro = province_code) |>
  mutate(presented = "Yes")

# ------------------------------------------ one map per election, all provinces
vox_presence_regional_map <- esp_get_prov(epsg = "3857") |>
  cross_join(regional_elections |> distinct(election, election_label)) |>
  left_join(regional_elections |> distinct(election, cpro) |> mutate(voted = TRUE), by = c("election", "cpro")) |>
  left_join(vox_regional, by = c("election", "cpro")) |>
  mutate(presented = case_when(!is.na(presented) ~ "Yes",
                               voted             ~ "No",
                               TRUE              ~ "No election"),
         presented = factor(presented, levels = c("Yes", "No", "No election"))) |>
  # keep only elections where Vox skipped at least one province that voted
  group_by(election) |>
  filter(any(presented == "No")) |>
  ungroup()

vox_presence_regional <- ggplot(vox_presence_regional_map) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = presented), colour = "grey75", linewidth = 0.1) +
  geom_sf(data = esp_get_can_box(epsg = "3857"), fill = NA, colour = "grey60") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Yes" = "#009E73", "No" = "grey65", "No election" = "white"),
                    name = "Vox list") +
  facet_wrap(~ election_label, ncol = 2) +
  labs(title = "Regional elections where Vox did not run everywhere") +
  theme_void() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom",
        strip.text = element_text(size = 8))
```
