## Social Network

```{r EDGELIST CREATION}
library(tidyverse)

network_candidates <- vox_candidates |>
  mutate(
    contest = case_when(
      level == "National" ~ election,
      level == "Autonomical" ~ str_c(election, chamber, sep = " | "),
      level == "Municipal" ~ str_c(
        election,
        coalesce(province, ""),
        chamber,
        sep = " | "
      ),
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    ),
    # in municipal elections there are no CIS estimates, so the ex ante rule (previous
    # result in the same municipality) misses the local breakthrough of 2019: the head
    # of a list that won at least one councillor is also electable
    electable = coalesce(top_expected, FALSE) | coalesce(top_won, FALSE) |
      (level == "Municipal" & list_position == 1 & is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA) & is_elected %in% TRUE)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(contest), !is.na(person_id))

node_ids <- network_candidates |>
  filter(electable) |>
  distinct(person_id)

# ---- members of Vox's satellite organisations ---------------------------------------------
# every member is a node, whether or not they stood for Vox. The ones who did are matched
# with their candidate name, which is often longer ("IVAN VELEZ" is "ISMAEL IVAN VELEZ
# CIPRIANO"): the words of the member's name must appear in the candidate's name in the
# same order, with a middle name allowed after the first one
satellites <- c("DENAES", "Disenso", "ISSEP", "HazteOir", "CitizenGO", "Solidaridad", "Revuelta", "Homo Legens")

satellite_members <- people |>
  filter(organisation %in% satellites, str_count(person, " ") >= 1) |>
  distinct(organisation, person)

candidate_words <- network_candidates |>
  distinct(person_id) |>
  mutate(word = person_id) |>
  separate_longer_delim(word, " ") |>
  distinct()

# every candidate each member's name fits
satellite_fits <- satellite_members |>
  distinct(person) |>
  # particles are dropped from both names ("IGNACIO DE HOCES INIGUEZ" is "IGNACIO HOCES INIGUEZ")
  mutate(core = str_squish(str_remove_all(person, "\\b(DE|DEL|LA|LAS|LOS|Y)\\b")),
         word = word(core, -1)) |>
  inner_join(candidate_words, by = "word", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  mutate(candidate_core = str_squish(str_remove_all(person_id, "\\b(DE|DEL|LA|LAS|LOS|Y)\\b")),
         pattern = str_c("^(.*?)\\b", word(core, 1), "\\b(.*?)\\b", word(core, 2, -1), "\\b"),
         before  = str_match(candidate_core, pattern)[, 2],
         between = str_match(candidate_core, pattern)[, 3]) |>
  # the words before the member's first name and between it and the surname must be
  # forenames of the INE census ("ISMAEL IVAN VELEZ", "ANA MARIA VELASCO"), never surnames:
  # "SUSANA DIAZ" is not "SUSANA GARCIA DIAZ". A member named with more than one surname
  # is specific enough to skip the test ("HERMANN TERTSCH VALLELERSUNDI" is "HERMANN
  # LEOPOLD TERTSCH VALLELERSUNDI", and Leopold is not in the census)
  filter(!is.na(before),
         str_count(core, " ") >= 2 |
           map_lgl(str_split(str_squish(str_c(before, " ", between)), " "),
                   \(w) all(w %in% c("", census_forenames$forename)))) |>
  distinct(person, person_id) |>
  mutate(electable = person_id %in% node_ids$person_id)

# a name that fits several candidates ("RICARDO CHAMORRO": Delmo and Arevalo) goes to the
# one who was electable, if only one was; otherwise it is left out
satellite_matches <- satellite_fits |>
  filter(n() == 1 | (electable & sum(electable) == 1), .by = person)

# members matched to a candidate under a longer name: check them
satellite_matches |> filter(person != person_id) |> print(n = Inf)

# names that fit several candidates and were left out: check them by hand
satellite_fits |> filter(!person %in% satellite_matches$person) |> print(n = Inf)

# members who never stood for Vox, or did so under a name that could not be matched:
# look for the second kind here
satellite_members |> filter(!person %in% satellite_fits$person) |> arrange(organisation, person) |> print(n = Inf)

# each member with the id of their node: the candidate's if matched, their own otherwise
satellite_nodes <- satellite_members |>
  left_join(satellite_matches |> select(person, person_id), by = "person") |>
  mutate(person_id = coalesce(person_id, person))

# the members who stood for Vox join the candidacy network even if never electable
node_ids <- node_ids |>
  bind_rows(satellite_nodes |> filter(person_id %in% network_candidates$person_id) |> distinct(person_id)) |>
  distinct()

# ---- families of the previous parties, for the colours of the nodes ------------------
# the far right split as in the text (Casals): nostalgic Francoist and Falangist right,
# ultra-Catholic and traditionalist parties, national-populist right, neo-Nazi fringe
# and personalist vehicles; the mainstream parties apart
party_families <- tribble(
  ~party,     ~family,
  "PP",       "PP",
  "AP",       "PP",
  "Cs",       "Cs",
  "FN",       "Francoist / Falangist",
  "JJEE",     "Francoist / Falangist",
  "FE-JONS",  "Francoist / Falangist",
  "FA",       "Francoist / Falangist",
  "FE-2000",  "Francoist / Falangist",
  "LF",       "Francoist / Falangist",
  "ADÑ",      "Francoist / Falangist",
  "AES",      "Ultra-Catholic / traditionalist",
  "CTC",      "Ultra-Catholic / traditionalist",
  "DN",       "National-populist",
  "E2000",    "National-populist",
  "PxC",      "National-populist",
  "VD",       "National-populist",
  "SOMI",     "National-populist",
  "PxL",      "National-populist",
  "NOSOTROS", "National-populist",
  "HN",       "National-populist",
  "ADN",      "National-populist",
  "MSR",      "Neo-Nazi",
  "AN",       "Neo-Nazi",
  "GIL",      "Personalist populist",
  "ARM",      "Personalist populist",
  "CDS",      "Other right and centre",
  "PADE",     "Other right and centre",
  "UPN",      "Other right and centre",
  "Foro",     "Other right and centre",
  "PDP",      "Other right and centre",
  "AG",       "Other right and centre",
  "SCD",      "Other right and centre",
  "ACTUA",    "Other right and centre",   # Actúa Baleares
  "SR",       "Other right and centre",   # Somos Región (Murcia)
  "CiU",      "Other right and centre",
  "PSOE",     "Left",
  "PSC",      "Left",
  "PCE-EPK",  "Left"
)

# a candidate with several families keeps the first one in this order: a far-right past
# is kept over a mainstream one, being the rarer and more telling of the two
family_order <- c("Neo-Nazi", "Francoist / Falangist", "Ultra-Catholic / traditionalist",
                  "National-populist", "Personalist populist", "PP", "Cs",
                  "Other right and centre", "Left", "None")

# the palette to set in Gephi (Appearance > Nodes > Partition > prev_party_family)
family_colours <- c("Neo-Nazi"                        = "#000000",
                    "Francoist / Falangist"           = "#D55E00",
                    "Ultra-Catholic / traditionalist" = "#6A3D9A",
                    "National-populist"               = "#009E73",
                    "Personalist populist"            = "#F0E442",
                    "PP"                              = "#0072B2",
                    "Cs"                              = "#E69F00",
                    "Other right and centre"          = "#56B4E9",
                    "Left"                            = "#CC79A7",
                    "None"                            = "#D9D9D9")

# a member of a satellite organisation is coloured by the organisation instead
satellite_colours <- c("DENAES"      = "#8C510A",
                       "Disenso"     = "#DFC27D",
                       "ISSEP"       = "#E7298A",
                       "HazteOir"    = "#66A61E",
                       "CitizenGO"   = "#1B7837",
                       "Solidaridad" = "#A50026",
                       "Revuelta"    = "#FB9A99",
                       "Homo Legens" = "#01665E")

# parties without a family (must return 0 rows)
vox_candidates |>
  filter(!is.na(prev_party)) |>
  separate_longer_delim(prev_party, " | ") |>
  distinct(prev_party) |>
  filter(!prev_party %in% party_families$party)

vox_nodes <- network_candidates |>
  semi_join(node_ids, by = "person_id") |>
  group_by(person_id) |>
  summarise(
    name = first(candidate),
    contests = n_distinct(contest),
    contests_electable = n_distinct(contest[electable]),
    has_prev_party = any(coalesce(has_prev_party, FALSE)),
    prev_party = {
      x <- prev_party[
        coalesce(has_prev_party, FALSE) &
          !is.na(prev_party)
      ]
      x <- x |>
        str_split(fixed(" | ")) |>
        unlist() |>
        str_squish() |>
        unique() |>
        sort()
      if (length(x) == 0) NA_character_ else str_c(x, collapse = " | ")
    },
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_prev_parties = case_when(
      is.na(prev_party) ~ 0L,
      TRUE ~ str_count(prev_party, fixed(" | ")) + 1L
    ),
    # every family of the person's previous parties, and the one that colours the node
    prev_party_families = map_chr(str_split(replace_na(prev_party, ""), fixed(" | ")), \(p) {
      families <- party_families$family[party_families$party %in% p]
      if (length(families) == 0) "None" else str_c(intersect(family_order, families), collapse = " | ")
    }),
    prev_party_family = word(prev_party_families, 1, sep = fixed(" | "))
  ) |>
  # the members who never stood for Vox, as nodes of their own
  bind_rows(satellite_nodes |>
              filter(!person_id %in% network_candidates$person_id) |>
              distinct(person_id) |>
              mutate(name = str_to_title(person_id), contests = 0L, contests_electable = 0L,
                     has_prev_party = FALSE, n_prev_parties = 0L,
                     prev_party_families = "None", prev_party_family = "None")) |>
  # the satellite organisations of each node (in the order of `satellites`)
  left_join(satellite_nodes |>
              summarise(organisations = str_c(intersect(satellites, organisation), collapse = " | "),
                        .by = person_id),
            by = "person_id") |>
  mutate(satellite = !is.na(organisations),
         candidate = contests > 0,
         # the attribute that colours the node: the organisation for its members, the
         # family of the previous party for everybody else
         family    = if_else(satellite, word(organisations, 1, sep = fixed(" | ")), prev_party_family),
         colour    = unname(c(family_colours, satellite_colours)[family]))

participants <- network_candidates |>
  semi_join(node_ids, by = "person_id") |>
  group_by(contest, person_id) |>
  summarise(
    electable = any(electable),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

vox_edges <- participants |>
  inner_join(
    participants,
    by = "contest",
    suffix = c("_from", "_to"),
    relationship = "many-to-many"
  ) |>
  filter(
    person_id_from < person_id_to,
    electable_from | electable_to
  ) |>
  count(
    from = person_id_from,
    to = person_id_to,
    name = "weight"
  )

# members of the same satellite organisation are linked as well; a pair can be linked by
# both kinds of tie, recorded in `tie`
organisation_edges <- satellite_nodes |>
  distinct(organisation, person_id) |>
  inner_join(satellite_nodes |> distinct(organisation, person_id), by = "organisation",
             suffix = c("_from", "_to"), relationship = "many-to-many") |>
  filter(person_id_from < person_id_to) |>
  count(from = person_id_from, to = person_id_to, name = "weight")

vox_edges <- bind_rows(vox_edges |> mutate(tie = "candidacy"),
                       organisation_edges |> mutate(tie = "organisation")) |>
  summarise(weight = sum(weight), tie = str_c(sort(unique(tie)), collapse = " + "), .by = c(from, to))

vox_nodes |> count(family, colour, sort = TRUE)
vox_edges |> count(tie)

vox_nodes_gephi <- vox_nodes |>
  mutate(Id = as.character(person_id), Label = as.character(name)) |>
  select(Id, Label, family, prev_party, prev_party_family, prev_party_families, n_prev_parties,
         has_prev_party, organisations, satellite, candidate, contests, contests_electable, colour)

vox_edges_gephi <- vox_edges |>
  mutate(Source = as.character(from), Target = as.character(to),
         Type = "Undirected", Weight = as.numeric(weight)) |>
  select(Source, Target, Type, Weight, tie)

write_csv(vox_nodes_gephi, "vox_nodes_gephi.csv")
write_csv(vox_edges_gephi, "vox_edges_gephi.csv")
```

## Regressions

```{r EXPECTED SEATS VARIABLE AS A PREDICTOR}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)

# ---- 1. one row per VOX list (election + chamber + constituency) ----------------------
expected_check <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  group_by(level, election, chamber, province, expected_seats, expected_seats_source) |>
  summarise(seats = sum(is_elected %in% TRUE), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(from_cis = expected_seats_source == "CIS constituency estimate")

expected_check |> count(level, expected_seats_source)

# ---- 2. do the expected seats predict the seats actually won? --------------------------
# standard errors clustered by election: constituencies of the same election share shocks
models <- list(
  "1 Pooled"      = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = expected_check),
  "2 + level FE"  = lm(seats ~ expected_seats + level, data = expected_check),
  "3 + source"    = lm(seats ~ expected_seats * from_cis + level, data = expected_check),
  "4 National"    = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "National")),
  "5 Autonomical" = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "Autonomical")),
  "6 Municipal"   = lm(seats ~ expected_seats, data = filter(expected_check, level == "Municipal"))
)

regression_table <- list()
for (m in names(models)) {
  regression_table[[m]] <- coeftest(models[[m]],
                                    vcov = vcovCL(models[[m]], cluster = ~ election)) |>
    tidy() |>
    mutate(model = m,
           n     = nobs(models[[m]]),
           r2    = summary(models[[m]])$r.squared)
}
regression_table <- bind_rows(regression_table) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, p.value, n, r2) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, r2), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

regression_table |> print(n = Inf)

# ---- 3. the threshold: are the top_expected candidates the ones who got elected? --------
electable_check <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA)) |>
  mutate(is_elected = is_elected %in% TRUE)

electable_logit <- glm(is_elected ~ top_expected + level,
                       family = binomial, data = electable_check)

coeftest(electable_logit, vcov = vcovCL(electable_logit, cluster = ~ election)) |>
  tidy() |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate))

# share elected among top_expected and the rest
electable_check |>
  group_by(level, top_expected) |>
  summarise(candidates = n(), elected = sum(is_elected),
            share_elected = mean(is_elected), .groups = "drop")

# ---- 4. plot: expected seats against seats won -------------------------------------------
ggplot(expected_check, aes(expected_seats, seats)) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_jitter(aes(colour = expected_seats_source), width = 0.1, height = 0.1, alpha = 0.5, size = 1.6) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", se = TRUE, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ level, scales = "free") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("CIS constituency estimate"          = "#0072B2",
                                 "previous result, same constituency" = "#E69F00",
                                 "no CIS estimate before 2018 (0)"    = "#CC79A7",
                                 "first contest (0)"                  = "#999999")) +
  labs(x = "Expected seats", y = "Seats actually won", colour = NULL,
       title = "Do the expected seats predict the seats Vox actually won?",
       subtitle = "One point per list. Dashed line: perfect prediction.") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())
```

```{r REGRESSION SEX}
library(sandwich)
library(lmtest)
library(broom)
library(survival)

# Who gets an electable place? The Congress candidates of July 2023 are split in two
# groups by ISCO_CANDIDATOS_VOX_2023.xlsx (isco08_group): those within the electoral
# threshold of their constituency ("Dentro del umbral", the heads of list included) and
# the three titulars right below it ("Justo debajo del umbral"), who are neither heads
# of list nor above the threshold in that election. One row per person
threshold_sample <- vox_candidates |>
  filter(election == "general_2023_07", chamber == "Congress",
         is_titular %in% c(TRUE, NA), !is.na(isco08_group)) |>
  slice_min(list_position, n = 1, by = person_id, with_ties = FALSE) |>
  mutate(electable      = isco08_group == "Dentro del umbral",
         sex            = factor(sex, levels = c("Male", "Female")),
         isco_class     = case_when(isco08_major == "1"  ~ "1 Managers",
                                    isco08_major == "2"  ~ "2 Professionals",
                                    !is.na(isco08_major) ~ "3 Rest",
                                    TRUE                 ~ "4 Unknown") |>
                            factor(levels = c("3 Rest", "1 Managers", "2 Professionals", "4 Unknown")),
         prev_party_any = has_prev_party %in% TRUE) |>
  select(person_id, candidate, province, list_position, electable, isco08_group, sex,
         isco08, isco08_title, isco08_major, isco08_major_title, isco_class,
         prev_party, prev_party_any, in_lists_2013_2017)

threshold_sample |> count(isco08_group, electable)

# the constituencies that identify the comparison: those with people in both groups
threshold_sample |>
  summarise(within = sum(electable), below = sum(!electable), .by = province) |>
  arrange(desc(within)) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# ---- 1. sex: descriptives and Fisher exact test ----------------------------------------
sex_table <- table(sex = threshold_sample$sex, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
sex_table
prop.table(sex_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(sex_table)

# ---- 2. sex as a predictor of an electable place ----------------------------------------
# the odds of an electable place are compared in two ways:
#   a. a logit over the whole sample, standard errors clustered by constituency
#   b. a conditional logit, which compares the candidates of the same constituency only
#      (constituencies with no electable candidate drop out of this model)
# list_position is not a control here: the two groups are defined by it
threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit"             = glm(electable ~ sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Conditional logit" = clogit(electable ~ sex + strata(province), data = threshold_sample)
)

# the table of every model: clustered standard errors for the logits, the model's own for
# the conditional logit, which is already within constituency
threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)
```

```{r REGRESSION ISCO + SEX}
# The occupation before politics (ISCO-08 major group) added to sex. The four digit codes
# are collapsed into managers (1), professionals (2), the rest (3-9) and "Unknown", the
# candidates whose occupation was not found: they are 2 of the 44 within the threshold and
# 61 of the 137 below it, so the category also measures how much press each group gets
threshold_sample |> count(electable, isco_class)
threshold_sample |> count(electable, isco08_major, isco08_major_title) |> print(n = Inf)

isco_table <- table(isco = threshold_sample$isco_class, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
isco_table
prop.table(isco_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(isco_table)

# the same, dropping the candidates without a known occupation
fisher.test(isco_table[rownames(isco_table) != "4 Unknown", ])

threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit, ISCO"            = glm(electable ~ isco_class, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Logit, ISCO + sex"      = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "3 Conditional logit"      = clogit(electable ~ isco_class + sex + strata(province), data = threshold_sample),
  "4 Logit, ISCO known only" = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex, family = binomial,
                                   data = filter(threshold_sample, isco_class != "4 Unknown"))
)

threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)
```


```{r REGRESSION ISCO + SEX + PREV_PARTY}
# A previous party added to the occupation and sex. has_prev_party is TRUE or NA, because
# the absence of a previous party cannot be told apart from the absence of evidence of one;
# to compare the two groups every NA is read here as FALSE (prev_party_any, built with the
# sample), so the coefficient is the effect of a previous party *on record*
threshold_sample |> count(electable, prev_party_any)
threshold_sample |> filter(prev_party_any) |> count(electable, prev_party) |> print(n = Inf)

party_table <- table(prev_party = threshold_sample$prev_party_any, electable = threshold_sample$electable)
party_table
prop.table(party_table, margin = 1) |> round(3)
fisher.test(party_table)

threshold_models <- list(
  "1 Logit, party"              = glm(electable ~ prev_party_any, family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "2 Logit, ISCO + sex + party" = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any,
                                      family = binomial, data = threshold_sample),
  "3 Conditional logit"         = clogit(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + strata(province),
                                         data = threshold_sample),
  "4 + lists of 2013-2017"      = glm(electable ~ isco_class + sex + prev_party_any + in_lists_2013_2017,
                                      family = binomial, data = threshold_sample)
)

threshold_table <- list()
for (m in names(threshold_models)) {
  threshold_table[[m]] <- (if (inherits(threshold_models[[m]], "coxph"))
                             tidy(threshold_models[[m]])
                           else
                             coeftest(threshold_models[[m]],
                                      vcov = vcovCL(threshold_models[[m]], cluster = ~ province)) |>
                               tidy()) |>
    mutate(model = m, n = nobs(threshold_models[[m]]))
}
threshold_table <- bind_rows(threshold_table) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate)) |>
  select(model, term, estimate, std.error, odds_ratio, p.value, n) |>
  mutate(across(c(estimate, std.error, odds_ratio), \(x) round(x, 3)),
         p.value = signif(p.value, 3))

threshold_table |> print(n = Inf)

# an odds ratio in the thousands with a huge standard error means a category has no
# variation left (complete separation): read the Fisher tables above instead
```

```{r CIS 2019 POLITICAL DETERMINANTS OF VOX SUPPORT}
library(haven)

# Figure 4.12 of the literature (average marginal effect of the political determinants of
# the support for Vox) rebuilt with the microdata of the postelectoral survey of the general
# election of November 2019: CIS, study 3269 (CIS 2019b)
cis_file <- "MD3269/3269.sav"

if (!file.exists(cis_file)) {
  zip_file <- "MD3269.zip"
  download.file("https://www.cis.es/documents/d/cis/MD3269", zip_file, mode = "wb",
                method = "libcurl", headers = c("User-Agent" = "Mozilla/5.0"))
  unzip(zip_file, exdir = "MD3269", junkpaths = TRUE)
}

cis_2019 <- read_sav(cis_file)

# ---- 1. the variables of the figure ------------------------------------------------------
# B22R      vote recalled in November 2019 (18 = VOX); blank, void, abstention and no answer out
# C3        left-right self-placement, 1 (left) to 10 (right)
# C12A      attendance at religious services: "frequent" is every Sunday or more often; the
#           non-believers, who are not asked about it, do not attend
# B1        interest in politics: "a lot" or "quite a lot"
# B20       did what happened in Catalonia have an effect on your vote? (self-reported)
# A9_1..3   the three most important problems of Spain: 18 immigration, 45 independence of
#           Catalonia. The figure is reproduced with a problem named in any of the three
#           answers; naming it first is the robustness check below
# B30       national identity: "I feel only Spanish" is the exclusionary one
# controls: sex, age, subjective class, education, household income, size of the
#           municipality (the smaller, the more rural) and fixed effects of the autonomous
#           community. Class, education and income keep a "N.C." level, so that the item
#           non-response (40% of the income question) does not empty the sample, and the
#           income brackets are grouped: with the raw ones nobody in the lowest voted VOX
vox_support <- cis_2019 |>
  mutate(vote                = as.numeric(B22R),
         vox                 = as.integer(vote == 18),
         left_right          = if_else(C3 <= 10, as.numeric(C3), NA),
         church_attendance   = case_when(C12A %in% c(5, 6) ~ 1L, C12A == 9 ~ NA_integer_, TRUE ~ 0L),
         political_interest  = case_when(B1 %in% c(1, 2) ~ 1L, B1 %in% c(3, 4) ~ 0L, TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
         catalan_effect      = case_when(B20 == 1 ~ 1L, B20 == 2 ~ 0L, TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
         problem_immigration = as.integer(A9_1 == 18 | A9_2 == 18 | A9_3 == 18) |> replace_na(0L),
         problem_catalonia   = as.integer(A9_1 == 45 | A9_2 == 45 | A9_3 == 45) |> replace_na(0L),
         first_immigration   = as.integer(A9_1 == 18),
         first_catalonia     = as.integer(A9_1 == 45),
         spanish_only        = case_when(B30 == 1 ~ 1L, B30 %in% c(2, 3, 4, 5, 7) ~ 0L, TRUE ~ NA_integer_),
         female              = as.integer(C9 == 2),
         age                 = as.numeric(C10),
         class               = factor(if_else(CLASESUB %in% 1:5, as.character(CLASESUB), "N.C.")),
         education           = factor(if_else(ESTUDIOS %in% 1:6, as.character(ESTUDIOS), "N.C.")),
         income              = case_when(C19 %in% 1:4  ~ "1 up to 900",
                                         C19 %in% 5:6  ~ "2 901-1800",
                                         C19 %in% 7:8  ~ "3 1801-3000",
                                         C19 %in% 9:11 ~ "4 over 3000",
                                         TRUE          ~ "5 N.C.") |> factor(),
         rurality            = 8 - as.numeric(TAMUNI),
         ccaa                = factor(as.numeric(CCAA)),
         weight              = as.numeric(PESO)) |>
  filter(!is.na(vote), !vote %in% c(77, 96, 97, 98, 99)) |>
  select(vox, left_right, church_attendance, political_interest, catalan_effect,
         problem_immigration, problem_catalonia, first_immigration, first_catalonia,
         spanish_only, female, age, class, education, income, rurality, ccaa, weight) |>
  drop_na(vox, left_right, church_attendance, political_interest, catalan_effect,
          problem_immigration, problem_catalonia, first_immigration, first_catalonia,
          spanish_only, female, age, rurality)

cat("voters:", nrow(vox_support), " VOX:", sum(vox_support$vox),
    " share:", round(100 * mean(vox_support$vox), 1), "%\n")

vox_support |>
  summarise(n = n(),
            across(c(left_right, church_attendance, political_interest, catalan_effect,
                     problem_immigration, problem_catalonia, spanish_only), \(x) round(mean(x), 3)),
            .by = vox)

# ---- 2. logit of the vote for Vox ---------------------------------------------------------
# the unweighted logit is the model of the figure; the other two are checks: the same model
# with the weights of the survey, and with the problem named in the first place only
vox_models <- list(
  "1 Logit"          = glm(vox ~ left_right + church_attendance + political_interest +
                             catalan_effect + problem_immigration + problem_catalonia +
                             spanish_only + female + age + class + education + income +
                             rurality + ccaa,
                           family = binomial, data = vox_support),
  "2 Weighted"       = glm(vox ~ left_right + church_attendance + political_interest +
                             catalan_effect + problem_immigration + problem_catalonia +
                             spanish_only + female + age + class + education + income +
                             rurality + ccaa,
                           family = quasibinomial, data = vox_support, weights = weight),
  "3 First problem"  = glm(vox ~ left_right + church_attendance + political_interest +
                             catalan_effect + first_immigration + first_catalonia +
                             spanish_only + female + age + class + education + income +
                             rurality + ccaa,
                           family = binomial, data = vox_support)
)

tidy(vox_models[["1 Logit"]]) |>
  filter(!str_detect(term, "^(ccaa|class|education|income)")) |>
  mutate(odds_ratio = exp(estimate), across(where(is.numeric), \(x) signif(x, 3)))

# the Basque Country has no VOX voter in the sample, so its fixed effect is separated and
# its 110 respondents get a predicted probability of zero
vox_support |> summarise(vox = sum(vox), n = n(), .by = ccaa) |> arrange(vox) |> head(3)

# ---- 3. average marginal effects, in percentage points ------------------------------------
# for the dummies, the average change of the predicted probability between 1 and 0; for the
# left-right scale, the average slope of one point of the scale. The confidence intervals
# are drawn from the coefficients (1000 draws of a normal with the estimated variance matrix)
political_terms <- c("Left-right position"                          = "left_right",
                     "(Frequent) church attendance"                 = "church_attendance",
                     "Political interested"                         = "political_interest",
                     "Catalan crisis had an effect (self-reported)" = "catalan_effect",
                     "Most important problem = Immigration"         = "problem_immigration",
                     "Most important problem = Catalan crisis"      = "problem_catalonia",
                     "Exclusionary Spanish identity"                = "spanish_only")

set.seed(20191110)
margins <- list()
for (m in names(vox_models)) {
  design <- model.matrix(vox_models[[m]])
  beta   <- coef(vox_models[[m]])
  draws  <- t(MASS::mvrnorm(1000, beta, vcov(vox_models[[m]])))

  for (label in names(political_terms)) {
    v <- political_terms[[label]]
    if (m == "3 First problem") v <- str_replace(v, "^problem", "first")
    if (v == "left_right") {                      # continuous: the average derivative
      effects <- colMeans(dlogis(design %*% draws) * rep(draws[v, ], each = nrow(design)))
      point   <- mean(dlogis(design %*% beta) * beta[[v]])
    } else {                                      # dummy: the average discrete change
      design1 <- design; design1[, v] <- 1
      design0 <- design; design0[, v] <- 0
      effects <- colMeans(plogis(design1 %*% draws) - plogis(design0 %*% draws))
      point   <- mean(plogis(design1 %*% beta) - plogis(design0 %*% beta))
    }
    margins[[str_c(m, label)]] <- tibble(model = m, term = label,
                                         ame       = 100 * point,
                                         conf_low  = 100 * quantile(effects, 0.025),
                                         conf_high = 100 * quantile(effects, 0.975))
  }
}
margins <- bind_rows(margins) |>
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = rev(names(political_terms))))

margins |>
  mutate(across(c(ame, conf_low, conf_high), \(x) round(x, 2))) |>
  arrange(model, desc(term)) |>
  print(n = Inf)

# ---- 4. the figure ------------------------------------------------------------------------
ggplot(filter(margins, model == "1 Logit"), aes(ame, term)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey75", linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_linerange(aes(xmin = conf_low, xmax = conf_high), colour = "grey35") +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, colour = "grey20") +
  geom_text(aes(label = str_replace(as.character(signif(ame, 2)), "^(-?)0", "\\1")),
            vjust = -1.1, size = 3, family = "serif") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-5, 15), breaks = seq(-5, 15, 5)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       title = "Political determinants of support for VOX",
       caption = str_c("Confidence intervals (95%) | Controls not illustrated: gender, age, ",
                       "class (self-reported), education, income, rurality, CCAA fixed effects\n",
                       "Average marginal effects on the probability of voting VOX, in percentage ",
                       "points. Own elaboration with CIS study 3269 (2019b), n = ", nrow(vox_support))) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11, base_family = "serif") +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 12),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, size = 7, colour = "grey30"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_line(linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey80"),
        axis.line.x = element_line(colour = "grey40"),
        axis.ticks.x = element_line(colour = "grey40"),
        plot.margin = margin(10, 20, 10, 10))
```
